 Game Coverage: Watch Listen Live Stats Game Notes No. 11/12 Lehigh Returns to PL Play at Villanova Saturday
 10/20/2026 2:32:00 PM | Football
 Game Notes Watch on ESPN+ Listen on FOX Sports Radio Live Stats Share: BETHLEHEM, Pa. – After suffering its first loss of the season and seeing a 23-game regular season winning streak come to an end, No. 11/12 Lehigh heads down the Main Line to face Villanova Saturday at 3:30 p.m. in the first of five straight Patriot League games to end the regular season. This will be the first meeting between the Mountain Hawks and Wildcats as league foes. Villanova defeated Lehigh 14-7 in the second round of the 2025 FCS playoffs at Goodman Stadium. Lehigh scored 38 points, including three touchdown passes by sophomore Derek Morgan , but an uncharacteristically tough day for the defense resulted in a 48-38 loss at Cornell last Saturday. Senior Luke Yoder rushed for 142 yards and his 13th touchdown of the season. Villanova came off its bye with a 38-17 win at Fordham to even its league record at 2-2.
Lehigh's first touchdown at Cornell came on a 100-yard fumble return by junior safety Luke Denny . Cornell quarterback Garrett Bass-Sulpizio was stripped by first-year Cayden Vassa at the one-yard line with Denny collecting the loose ball in the end zone and racing 100 yards to paydirt. The 100-yard fumble return ties the school record, set by Steve Smoke against Penn State in 1938.
The Lehigh defense, which ranked among the nation's best, had an uncharacteristically tough day at Cornell. The Mountain Hawks allowed their most points and yards since 2023. Lehigh allowed just four touchdowns in the first three quarters of its first six games, but Cornell scored five in the first 45 minutes against the Mountain Hawks. Despite its showing at Cornell, Lehigh still ranks in the top 10 in the FCS in rushing defense (102.3), scoring defense (17.0), interceptions (10) and takeaways (15).
With the loss of Lehigh's top two receivers from a season ago, including Geoffrey Jamiel , who ranks in the top five in program history for career receptions and receiving yards, the Mountain Hawks have relied on a number of younger receivers to contribute so far this season. Lehigh quarterbacks have completed passes to 12 different receivers through seven games. Junior Nick Palumbo leads Lehigh with 18 receptions and three touchdowns, while gaining 227 yards. Sophomore Anthony Feaster leads with 276 yards and scored his first two career touchdowns against Fordham. Jamaire Harden , Luke Yoder , Joseph Marranca , Aiden Schomp and Bryce Werner also have touchdown catches this season.
A national semifinalist a season ago, Villanova is 3-4 overall and 2-2 in Patriot League play this season. The Wildcats are coming off their best performance of the season in a 38-17 win at Fordham last Saturday. Quarterback Pat McQuaide threw for 235 yards and two touchdowns, while rushing for a third. Isaiah Ragland and Ja'briel Mace both rushed for first quarter touchdowns in the win. Both backs have over 400 rushing yards this season. Omari Bursey is the top tackler with 77 stops. Villanova is still searching for its first home win in 2026 following losses to William & Mary, Colgate and Morgan State.
Lehigh and Villanova will meet for the 21st time, with the Wildcats holding a 15-5 edge in the series. Villanova has won the last 12 meetings. Lehigh's last win in the series came back in 2006, by a 31-28 score. This will be Lehigh's seventh visit to Villanova since the series resumed in 2004 (2006, 2008, 2009, 2016, 2019, 2022). Lehigh won the first four meetings (1903, 1914, 1919 and 1924), while Villanova won in 1925 and 1927 prior to the 77-year break in the series.
Villanova is one of two new members of Patriot League football with the Wildcats and William & Mary joining the league as associate members this year. Lehigh has defeated the last five newcomers to Patriot League football in the first meeting as league foes, including its 44-20 win over William & Mary on Sept. 12. In 1989, Lehigh opened its season with a win at Fordham. The Mountain Hawks won at Towson in 1997. Lehigh welcomed Georgetown to the Patriot League with a 41-14 victory in 2001. Last year, the Mountain Hawks defeated Richmond 21-14.
Saturday's game kicks off just after 3:30 p.m. from Villanova Stadium. The game will be broadcast on ESPN+ with audio coverage will be available on FOX Sports Radio 94.7 FM and 1230 AM and LVFOXSports.com.
Lehigh will play its next two games at Goodman Stadium, beginning next Saturday, when the Mountain Hawks host Bucknell on Hawk-o-Ween: A Spooky Saturday at Goodman, with game time set for noon. The Mountain Hawks host Colgate in the regular season home finale on Nov. 7.

 •Senior running back Luke Yoder needs 44 rushing yards to reach 1,000 for the third time in his career. He would join Dom Bragalone '19 as the only Lehigh rushers with three 1,000-yard rushing seasons. Yoder also needs 302 yards to break Bragalone's career rushing record.
